summary: The swap, the no-exo, citation and sign-code findings are right. The divisor evidence is stated with a circular method, and one converter bug is missing. With the bias b estimated from the same 6 trials under the worn hypothesis (0.98), body mass fits only 1/6. With b free per hypothesis, body mass also fits 5/6 (own median 0.889). The C02 slopes alone therefore cannot separate worn from body mass. They do favour the worn mass if the GT23-calibrated lever bias (GT23-C04 ankle_bias_centre_ratio 0.9942) transfers to GT24: then worn fits 6/6 and body 1/6. The audit should rest on that external calibration and state the transfer assumption. 'Body mass ruled out' should be softened. Because the decision's premise and its option C factors assume a worn divisor, D-GT24-C01-1 should be queued until the E1 pilot reports.

checks.result: sound and bounded, with one interpretive caveat
evidence: Rules are fixed before any data are read.
E1 is exact when the robust relative spread is <= 1e-3 and |corr| >= 0.9999, with a second identity through power. E2 is plate weight. E3 is the lever arm with the GT23 band.
58 seeded trials (seed 20261031) in 25 folders; zip members read one at a time without extraction; RLIMIT_AS 1.5 GiB; launcher-only. The 78 tests (71 backlog + synthetic probe) pass.

Caveat: E1 identifies the divisor used to convert torque_interaction when bio = net - interaction / D. It equals the net-moment divisor only if the authors used the same mass for both. E3 is the check for that, and it carries the same bias-transfer assumption as check 1. Say so in the probe's reading.
